content: Hydralazine is available in oral tablet forms of 10 mg, 25 mg, 50 mg, and 100 mg. It is also supplied in injectable forms for administration into a blood vessel or muscle. Hydralazine should be stored at room temperature, specifically between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). It can tolerate short-term exposure to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C), such as during transportation. Always store it in a cool, dry place and ensure the container is tightly closed. The most common side effects of hydralazine include headache, decreased appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, a pounding or rapid heartbeat, and chest pain or discomfort. If any of these side effects become bothersome, inform your healthcare provider. There may be additional side effects not listed here, so contact your healthcare provider if you suspect you are experiencing any adverse effects. Serious side effects of hydralazine, though less common, include lupus-like symptoms, chest pain, blood disorders, and nerve problems. Lupus-like symptoms may present as rash, joint pain, fever, weakness, swollen glands, reduced urination, or discolored urine (pink, red, or brown). If you experience any of these, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Chest pain caused by hydralazine could indicate a heart attack, especially in individuals with pre-existing heart disease. Seek emergency medical attention if you experience chest pain, pressure, abnormal heartbeat, difficulty breathing, pain radiating to the back, jaw, throat, or arm, or symptoms like sweating, nausea, vomiting, or dizziness. Blood disorders such as agranulocytosis, anemia, or leukopenia may manifest as fever, shortness of breath, pale or yellowish skin, easy bruising or bleeding, frequent infections, or unusual fatigue. Notify your healthcare provider if you experience these symptoms. Peripheral neuropathy, or nerve damage, may also occur, leading to altered sensations. Hydralazine should not be used by individuals allergic to hydralazine, Apresoline, or any of the ingredients in the specific product. Consult your pharmacist for a complete list of ingredients. It is contraindicated in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD) or mitral valvular rheumatic heart disease. In CAD, hydralazine’s blood pressure-lowering effect can increase the workload on the heart, potentially leading to a heart attack. In mitral valvular disease, the increased blood flow to the heart caused by hydralazine can strain the mitral valve. Do not take hydralazine unless prescribed by a healthcare provider. Follow the prescribed dosage and do not share the medication with others, even if they have similar conditions. Keep hydralazine out of reach of children. Be aware that hydralazine may affect alertness or coordination, so avoid driving or engaging in activities requiring focus until you know how it affects you. Before using hydralazine, inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions, including heart disease, kidney disease, stroke, or a history of rheumatic fever. Additionally, disclose all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking to avoid potential interactions. The effects of hydralazine on pregnancy are not well understood. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, consult your healthcare provider to determine if hydralazine is appropriate for you. Hydralazine passes into breast milk, so inform your healthcare provider if you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed. There are no known interactions between hydralazine and foods or non-alcoholic drinks. However, the risk of dizziness may increase if alcohol is consumed while taking hydralazine. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications and supplements you are using to avoid drug interactions. In case of an overdose, seek immediate medical attention by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take double or extra doses. Hydralazine is primarily used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and may be prescribed for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider. It works by relaxing blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more easily, which lowers blood pressure. This helps prevent complications such as heart or kidney problems, stroke, or heart attack.
